title: Data packs
summary: Signed folders of City open-data files, retrieved and compiled by the OnRecord pack builder, that you can import instead of downloading each table yourself.

paragraphs: A data pack holds the City's published files exactly as the pack builder downloaded them, with a signed manifest listing each file's address, retrieval time, size, SHA-256, row count and licence. Choose Data pack import in Analysis, then choose a pack's folder, or a pack OnRecord publishes.

sections.heading: Before anything is imported
items: The manifest's signature is checked, and the key that signed it must be the pack publisher key built into this app. A pack signed by any other key is refused, as is a manifest that lists a path outside the pack.
From a folder, every listed file must be inside it and match its listed size and SHA-256. One changed byte refuses the whole pack, and nothing from it is imported.

When you press Import, the manifest and each file you chose are checked again, and each file's digest once more as it is read, so a file changed after the check is refused too. If the pack's manifest is no longer the one you inspected, the import is refused; choose the folder again.

sections.heading: Published packs
items: OnRecord publishes its packs on Hugging Face, each in its own repository, Writerslogic/onrecord- followed by the pack's name. Choose one under Published packs; the app fetches only its signed manifest and checks it as above before showing what it holds.

Tables are listed with their years, rows and download sizes from the signed manifest. Some are hundreds of megabytes, and a whole pack can be several gigabytes, so nothing else is downloaded until you choose tables and years and press Download and import.

Each chosen file is downloaded into the app's own data folder and kept only if its size and SHA-256 match the signed manifest. A file that does not match is deleted, reported as failed, and nothing is imported from it; the files that matched are imported as from a folder. A file already downloaded and still matching is not downloaded again.

sections.heading: Choosing and importing
items: Files are listed by table and year, each with the date the pack builder retrieved it. Tick the ones you want; each becomes its own snapshot through the same analytical import as a file you fetch yourself. A file this app's City source list does not publish cannot be ticked.
A year marked as not over may gain rows after the pack was built. Its snapshot is recorded as partial.

Each result says what happened to that file: how many rows were imported and the date the pack builder retrieved it, that it held no readable rows, or that its bytes were already stored, in which case nothing is imported and the pack is recorded beside the existing snapshot. A file that fails is reported beside the others; the rest still import.

sections.heading: Where a snapshot came from
items: The pack, its version, build time, signing key, file path, SHA-256 and the builder's retrieval time are recorded beside the snapshot. A snapshot the pack created carries the builder's retrieval time as its own.

A file whose bytes are identical to one already imported from the same address stays one snapshot, so the two are never counted twice. Whichever comes first, the snapshot ends up describing your own fetch, and the pack is recorded beside it: a later fetch of the same bytes takes over a snapshot a pack created.

sections.heading: Licence
items: City of San Diego open data is published under the Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License (ODC-PDDL 1.0). The pack shows the licence and the City's disclaimer: the data is informational only, without warranty, and the City is not liable for any deficiency in it.
